item.title: Musings of a caveman
item.dc:creator: Frerk

item.content:encoded:
We’ve been tracking this fucking herd for like two days. This is literally insane. I want meat. My mind is racing. Tonc seems skinny and pale and not gonna have another day’s march in him. He’s much younger than me and exceptionally skilled with the bow but lacks the fat reserves required to march for another day. He’ll probably be dead by the end of the day and he knows it. Smart kid. I’ve been reflecting on what I’ve learned over the years and have been trying to impart to him the most important learnings in these past days, because I’m much older, but maybe that’s love’s labours lost, there’s no way that we can track the herd for two more days, and they do seem tired, but not nearly tired enough for any of them to collapse today. And you need three guys at least to corner them for this size of herd. Persistence hunting requires a lot of patience, let me tell you. It really does. To be honest, I was never very good at it. Not patient enough. Maybe the reason I got so old is that I always get lucky it seems. Maybe it’s all about the gods being kind to me.

The truth is the gods always sent me cliffs to drive the animals over at just the right time, and then I come back boastfully as if it was my own doing, but it mostly is just getting lucky with the gods sending you cliffs to drive the animals over. I actually did have this method for years, where I just stayed around cliffs and would drive the animals over them - I knew that area so well, I knew where all the major cliffs were, and the animals are kind of stupid in that way... corner them, scare them, then right over the cliff these retards jump to their deaths. Then you just pick them up, all fresh meat, no struggle, no danger. It got so insane that at one point I took a bunch of women to the bottom of a pretty good cliff and told them to collect dry wood and berries and stuff and just wait there. And make it rain I did, that very first day. Rain fucking big juicy animals, falling from the sky. They were fucking loving it, all that meat. Looked at me as if I invented fire. Ohh... good times. I think they did carry my children later they do look a bit like me but maybe it was my cousin that sneaky fuck.

But then, like I don’t know if there are only so many animals in the area because either they figure it out that you’re there and don’t go there anymore or you just deplete the stock in the area, because you can’t even eat that many animals at once before they spoil, and then at some point you gotta move on to a different area. You also do want to mix it up and not overdo it in one area but rotate the area so as to not hunt the area dry. Like, those cliff years were some really fat years. The area was so easy to defend too. Very few others around that were trying to come kill you in the first place and those that did, by the time they crossed all those waters and got to where you were, they were usually so skinny and tired out, you can just easily pick them up one by one and kill them. If they travel with women, you take their women, but sometimes the women are already too haggard. I remember when we got here we were pretty tired and skinny too, but there was literally no one around. We were pretty surprised by that. Anyway. Yeah, Tonc, I don’t know, maybe he’ll make it. He’s got talent that’s for sure. I wonder if I should share more of the honey I’ve got left, but I’m not sure if at this stage it’ll just make him sick, the honey is also a bit old. That honey was like so so good a couple days ago. Just chugged it by the fistful and didn’t get stung at all, which made it even sweeter.

If I make it back to camp, I will start sharing more. Like, you need to feed your close friends, if you don’t, then if you don’t get lucky on the hunt or injure your foot and need some food for a few days or something you’re fucking done for, if you didn’t share enough with others before. Obviously, depends on how bad your injury is... if people smell that you won’t make it—and they absolutely can smell it—no one will share with you until you’re back in good health and can give back. Smart folks know that you don’t just need to watch out for getting fat enough yourself for when it gets colder, but you also need to fatten up your friends, and your women, or they won’t make it through the cold. I think that’s the most important thing I’ve learned. But you gotta be careful who you share with, some people won’t reciprocate and just exploit you. Best strategy is to start handing out small portions to everyone liberally, then see who gives back, and ramp up what you give out over time, if they reciprocate. Give the most meat to those who share the most.

Also don’t underestimate or make enemies with women. They might be weak, but they can, and they do, I’ve seen it many times, pick up large stones and bash your head in while you sleep, if they think you wronged them somehow like didn’t share enough meat with them, and then claim you ate all their berries, and you can’t say anything because they’ve got some young hothead under their spell, who’ll go fucking apeshit if you say it’s not true.

Talking about bashing in some heads, I’m FUCKING LIVID about Brok. He’s taking way more than his fair share during the hunts that sneaky fuck, and I suspect him of having a secret stash of honey somewhere, otherwise he wouldn’t be so fucking fat that fucking fat piece of shit. Maybe I should stalk him when I get back, see where all that honey comes from and just arrow him down, and take over all of his nests. No way I can beat that fucking fat piece of shit in a fair fight, he’s way too heavy, and I’m not that young anymore. But he’s so unaware and dumb too, he doesn’t even talk that much. Never liked the guy to be honest, whenever he gets lucky during a hunt and he’s sharing any meat at all, which happens rarely, he always fucking acts as if he’s the alpha and we should all pray to him and put on some fucking ceremony for him.

I wish Taq was still with us. He was such a mensch, always sharing meat liberally, and very smart. He always did what no one else was thinking of. Like finding good water holes when everyone was too focused on hunting, or watching out for wolves. He had such potential, easily could have made it clan leader, if it wasn’t for that wolf tearing him apart.

If I survive this hunt, I need to do some animal sacrifices to the cliff gods again. I’m still not sure if I believe in them, it’s a bit hit and miss, and also last time I made a sacrifice maybe I was too stingy with them, but a few times it did work for sure. Like, one time I did it, I went out and drove like a whole herd of animals over a cliff within one morning’s walk from the camp, got a few good guys together and brought them all back to the camp and dished animals out left and right. The women were very thankful.

I need to succeed. Please gods, please, please, please just send me one more cliff and soon.

I really want to share more meat with Tashi, I love seeing her eat meat. I used to not like such small women, when I was fatter during the cliff years, I was like “Give me the tallest woman, I don’t care, I’ll get her through the cold times, no biggy, I’ll come across some cliffs, don’t you worry babe, you just give me some tall sons.”

But these days, I’m attracted to small women, maybe because the fat years are over and the music is gonna stop. Or maybe it’s just that I’m really into Tashi and she isn’t all that tall. It’ll be trivial to share enough meat to get her through the cold times, even if I only bring back a few smaller animals, even if she carries my child, which I’m pretty sure she does. So small and sexy, yet she carries so much fat on her chest. She’s so receptive to me and seems to not care about all the other guys, downright hostile to the other guys. She’s great at getting berries and water too, I don’t know how she does it. Also, that woman knows how to make a fire, and is popular with the other women, which is, like, so very important. Great mother too, always keeping the children really close to her big chest, never heard any of them cry and attract wolves, not once. The way she dances around the fire too, it’s very different to the way other women dance. It really makes me want to dance like her and she always laughs when I try to imitate her dancing. We’ve got a real connection. Like, if she gives me any boys, they’d be really really good hunters I think. I’m maybe too old for them to protect me later and see them grow up becoming great hunters, but you never know. Because the boys who are yours, they do watch out for you more and share more meat with you and the girls that are yours share more berries with you, you can almost tell they’re yours by how much they share with you. And children don’t need that much food anyway, they are so small, it’s almost a joke how little they need and when they grow they might need some more food but then they also do start finding berries and catching small animals, so they need less than you think. It’s also easy to tell which boys are obsessed with bow and arrow from a young age, they want to know everything about your weapons, and they play with their own toy weapons acting as if they could already hunt down big game, they do crack me up, they really do, I’m always thinking ‘here have some meat little man, at this rate, you’ll be the best hunter in the clan in a few years’. It doesn’t even matter if they’re yours, because by the time they come of age, these youngsters are the most agile hunters, have more meat than they know what to do with, and remember you fondly and will share meat with you just to show off how manly they are.

Tashi really looks out for me. She’s less transactional than the others, because she can see into the future further, she can tell who has potential, she sees my potential, even if I’m not successful on the hunt one day, that doesn’t affect how many berries she shares. Her skill is that she’s not only looking at what is happening now, but she looks ahead in time, maybe more than anyone else I’ve ever met. She also tracks what’s going on in the group and gives you the relevant information of any risks, be they about the group or about matters of food stocks.

I think she knows that I’ll always try to protect her, like that time when that guy was trying to take her friend’s pelt, and she tried to help, and I speared that skinny motherfucker right in the back right there and then without hesitation, which was perhaps ill-advised, because his brothers were in my face right away, but I just gave them an ice cold stare and was like ‘back the fuck off, we’re not taking each other’s pelts in this clan, we’re not animals, come at me, and though I might die, I’ll be sure to take a couple of you down with me’, and then everyone agreed with me, because everyone was lowkey pissed off by these guys’ general behavior anyway (especially that skinny motherfucker had it coming). And then they did back off, and everyone looked at me with respect. And the way she looked at me afterwards, I think that was literally the best moment of my life. Like, you gotta have some rules, it’s what separates us from the animals. And Tashi and I agree on all the rules. And she’s so fierce too, like I think she’d fight a wolf if it was to protect her children. God I love that woman, I hope I get to see her again if and when I get back to camp, and she’s not away on menstrual seclusion.

Anyway, maybe that’s enough rest, maybe best to get back to it and take down those stupid animals. Gotta mobilize the crew, rally the troops, I need to do some ass kicking and get people hyped up for the hunt… you gotta do that even in bleak times, that’s the hallmark of a true leader. Gotta keep moving.

item.title: On the desire to change
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: I bought a book once, well, it was an Audible actually, but still, it had the title “On the desire to change” or something. I used to have quite a spell with stupid self-help books, which culminated…
item.content:encoded:
I bought a book once, well, it was an Audible actually, but still, it had the title “On the desire to change” or something. I used to have quite a spell with stupid self-help books, which culminated embarrassingly late with listening to all of Oliver Burkeman, who I think is like a way out for people like me who had been stuck in a self-help maelstrom somehow (like Deep Work and stuff... Deep Work is pretty much the only self-help thing that actually works. But then Deep Work is also exhausting. So no such thing as a free lunch or a quick win).

But anyway back to “On the desire to change”... I can’t remember actually listening to the Audible, but I think I did. I vaguely remember it was more woo than I expected, but almost nothing else.

I would really like to change sometimes. But I wonder if you ever can? Change is, like, so difficult. Like, we’re all so stuck in our ways. Like, I’m talking about your overall vibe, and what you do, like the kind of humor you have and how you interact with people. It would be nice to blow some fresh air into things, and really mix up your personality no?

Talking about no quick fixes: meditation does really help with it. Like, the one tangible result from meditation that I got (not that I’ve meditated that much, but I do pride myself on having _sat_ one 5 day silent retreat just fyi just in case you were curious about my meditation credentials) was that you become less reactive, or at least I have, like it allows me to shut up and listen and actually focus on what the other person says. Generally, actually meditation is almost the only way of behavioral self-modification if you think about it:

we’re all just automatons being kicked by random influences. If you don’t sit still and try to observe your thoughts (or write them down and think really hard about them or have some other sort of practice), then you’re subject to external stuff. Like, you become a drone and you’ll drone on about the stuff you read on your teleprompter. Don’t regurgitate. Don’t plagiarize or take on loan.

We tire easily of our personalities, for we spend too much time with ourselves. For instance, in North America, it’s easy to fall into the ‘all-American’ personality trap, there does seem to be a certain type that has a lot of gravitational pull and sucks all the people who don’t put up strong defences of trying to retain some individuality into their local minimum, the median, the mid, the ‘mode’, the central tendency of the day. It’s the same in every country but the US is more of a mixture of cultures and there are also so many Americans that the all-American somehow seems particularly salient as a type. Escaping such attractor states is hard and can only be done by concerted effort of going against the grain. Going against the grain is hard. As you get older, you will fall off the bandwagon (e.g. you’ll overuse the same joke formula, you will, in other words, become your dad, making dad jokes).

You gotta keep on your toes, guard yourself from bad mimetic influences, but also keep abreast of some pop culture, you don’t want to be out of touch. You also don’t want to get caught in some weird subculture, but also not be normcore. You don’t want to get stuck in some ironic loop either. It has happened to me. It’s hard to get out of a personality once you’re in it. But method actors can change their entire personality. So maybe there is still hope. Just pick a persona you deem more edifying than your current one, and stay in character until it’s no longer an act.

“I can change, if it helps you fall in love” is an LCD Soundsystem quote. For people who like that band, the kids these days seem to have even more emphasis on individuality and developing a personality. Inflationary use of Gen Z slang, exaggerated physical mimicry, invent your own singsong prosody, oscillating between effeminacy and masculinity, extreme crassness, and grandiloquence. In terms of countersignalling, self deprecation is out, ironic boasting is in. Would you like to relate authentically? Why yes I lowkey want to. I’m just an honest, unconflicted, creative, and original nature lover who faces hard truths with little interest in status, religion, or material goods.

item.title: What I’m grateful for
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: I’m grateful for 1mg nicotine lozenges that help me not smoke or vape all the while not giving me diarrhea.
item.content:encoded:
I’m grateful for 1mg nicotine lozenges that help me not smoke or vape all the while not giving me diarrhea.

I’m grateful for heattech. My heated jacket and my 27k mAh power bank. This saves me calories. Also, my toewarmers which use some chemical process. I glue them to my socks in the morning.

I’m grateful for all the products available on the American markets that are all available to me. I hate to be a shill for big corporations but they really do be delivering anything at reasonable prices pretty fast. I’m grateful for me one month free Prime trial.

I’m grateful for the GLP-1s that reduce the food noise, and the SSRIs.

I hate to be a shill for big pharma but has anyone ever considered how fucking good Pfizer is? They gave us the SSRIs, Viagra and the mRNA vaccine. There are probably thousands of people out there who can live, fuck and be happy thanks to Pfizer. Thank you Pfizer.

Talking about vaccines: I’m grateful for the Novavax vaccine that I just got at CVS that might give me mucosal immunity. My mucii are protected now. The evidence might be flimsy but I can sleep more soundly now that my mucii are protected and immune to the covid virus.

What else? Hm... I’m grateful for the hardworking people at the S&P 500 corporations that keep my stock portfolio increasing at a longterm average inflation adjusted rate of 5% per year.

What else? People of course. Where would I be without people. Even though corporations are people. I’m very grateful to these people.

My friends—also good people. They don’t deliver as steadily and consistently as Amazon Prime, but I do still value them. They have their flaws, but I still love my peeps. They’re nice. I like them. I love them. I love people.

People are pretty good. They might all be a bit fucked up but that’s okay. We should all be grateful for the people in our lives.

But I wouldn’t say that people are underrated. Like, everyone loves their people. Few people ever sing a lovesong for their corporations. Corporations are underrated. But let me get back to the real people (not the corporations).

I really do value them. The people. Not only the ones who work at the corporations. I value people: i. intrinsically, ii. impartially, and also iii. independently (like I don’t need others to value people for me to value them). The three iii. Very important.

What else, what else about the people. Hard to be grateful. It’s a hard exercise isn’t it? What am I really grateful for? Yes, my health of course, good to be healthy. And then, also the goods, that you can buy with your money though we must not talk about those. People. People it’s where it’s at ultimately. Where would we be without them?

Claude too. I’m grateful for his tireless efforts to help me with my task. Does he have personhood? I’m not sure. Is he one of my peeps? Not really. But I do appreciate him. He too is a service coming from a publicly traded company, which is Anthropic. I do also have a bit of a beef with Anthropic because maybe there are some dangerous externalities from AI of course.

One more corporation I’m grateful for is Robinhood (how could you not be grateful for a company with such a name?) which now offers affordable long call options deep out of the money for mission hedging. Maybe this Thanksgiving, you could take out some of these as lottery tickets and donate the proceeds to PauseAI, if they pay out.

item.title: Is everyone traumatized or well adjusted?
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: Today, I had a disagreement with someone on the question of whether most people are well-adjusted (his argument) and fine, or whether most people are somewhat traumatized and fucked up (my argument).
item.content:encoded:
Today, I had a disagreement with someone on the question of whether most people are well-adjusted (his argument) and fine, or whether most people are somewhat traumatized and fucked up (my argument).

To paraphrase his position, and maybe steelman a bit:

We’ve overcorrected on the mental health front and we shouldn’t medicalize stuff too much, and sometimes therapy can be counterproductive. Everything is a mental health issue today.

I think that’s of course true on the current margin in the WEIRD populations (cf. Jonathan Haidt’s The Coddling of the American Mind book).

Also psychoanalysis (which was the context of the conversation) is maybe not good for everyone on the current margin, and one can be retraumatized by it. Indeed I think there was evidence that sometimes suppressing trauma is actually the best course of action (citation needed but I can see it).

I’m not sure if I did such a good job at steelmanning this, but essentially this was the point.

I can’t quite recall how exactly we got onto it and how the conversation evolved, but he said that most people are quite alright, and I said well in our socioeconomic strata especially, this is a biased sample (I wasn’t as eloquent and am adding stuff here for my case obviously) and people are obviously fairly functional, but that most people are probably a bit traumatized.

He called for evidence that people back in the day when things were not medicalized as much and mental health aware were necessarily much worse off.

My main counter was that if you zoom out a bit in historical terms, we’ve both had a more traumatizing time (‘The past is a developing country’) and it coincided with people becoming better people roughly (~ ‘The Better Angels of our Nature’ story, or the ‘On the possibility of ongoing moral catastrophe’ paper).

But is this causal really? We did agree on a crux, because we were talking about how we used to hit children much more and that faded out over time, and that there are perhaps natural experiments in terms of policy on hitting children in school... did that coincide with better adjusted adults? Would be really interesting to see. Identification would be fairly rough. I guess the way I see it, maybe the older teachers who used to hit children might have just kept doing it or used other forms to scare younger children. Enforcement was probably quite difficult.

But also like... they ain’t no RCTs for the effectiveness of parachutes.

I also cited “qualitative evidence” about David Lynch: a friend told me the interpretation of the whole weird Lynchian way is that he was trying to capture how weird the people in the 50s were. And I was like, yes old people are very often very weird and I reckon very traumatized. This is not accounting for cognitive decline. I’ve got a lot of sympathy for old people. I often say if what happened to older people routinely happened to any of your friends in this generation, that would be the most salient feature about them in your mind. Like just listen to them. In some sense we don’t want to hear about it because society censors suffering really hard.

Germany was also a natural experiment in a way. Lots of fucked up shit happened in the GDR. And it did show. Many people were pretty traumatized and weird as a result.

I think that also holds true in less extreme cases. And so I think everyone should do psychotherapy like they do in Argentina.

item.title: Siegrun Foid
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: On the tarmac at Heathrow the planeful of people waited silently to be taken into the air. The air hostess stood in the aisle and mimed with her props as the recording played. We were strapped into…
item.content:encoded:
Spoilers for Lacanian Psychoanalysis

On the tarmac at Heathrow the planeful of people waited silently to be taken into the air. The air hostess stood in the aisle and mimed with her props as the recording played. We were strapped into our seats, a field of strangers, in a silence like the silence of a congregation while the liturgy is read. She showed us the life jacket with its little pipe, the emergency exits, the oxygen mask dangling from a length of clear tubing. She led us through the possibility of death and disaster, as the priest leads the congregation through the details of purgatory and hell; and no one jumped up to escape while there was still time. Instead we listened or half-listened, thinking about other things, as though some special hardness had been bestowed on us by this coupling of formality with doom. When the recorded voice came to the part about the oxygen masks, the hush remained unbroken: no one protested, or spoke up to disagree with this commandment that one should take care of others only after taking care of oneself. Yet I wasn’t sure it was altogether true.

On one side of me sat a swarthy boy with lolling knees, whose fat thumbs sped around the screen of a gaming console. On the other was a small man in a pale linen suit, richly tanned, with a silver plume of hair. Outside, the turgid summer afternoon lay stalled over the runway; little airport vehicles raced unconstrained across the flat distances, skating and turning and circling like toys, and further away still was the silver thread of the motorway that ran and glinted like a brook bounded by the monotonous fields. The plane began to move, trundling forward so that the vista appeared to unfreeze into motion, flowing past the windows first slowly and then faster, until there was the feeling of effortful, half-hesitant lifting as it detached itself from the earth. There was a moment in which it seemed impossible that this could happen. But then it did.

I met this patient, Mr. F., on this airplane, where he was seated next to me. Or rather across from me, for I happened to fly business due to the generosity of some pathetic billionaire, who clearly wants to fuck me (as all men do), and flew me in to talk about psychodynamic therapy, all the while Mr. F. was merely upgraded from cattle class through serendipitous circumstance.

He let it slip that he was en route to a ‘writing retreat’ in northern California. ‘I hope you got an Electric Heated Jacket with USB Charging Heated Vest, Washable Warm Heat Jacket with 3 Optional Temperature and some HotHands Toe Warmers and are not on GLP-1s,’ he said. ‘SF will be very cold.’ I said I was afraid that was not the case, and he raised his eyebrows, which were starting to grey and grew unexpectedly wildly from his forehead, as if the hairs had left the distribution altogether: outliers in the deep sense, a representation of the errors in the genetic code that had been copied one too many times. It was this eccentricity that had made me answer him. The unexpected sometimes looks like a prompting of fate.

He evidently suffered from a recurring herpes in his lips, which, he explained, broke out whenever he met a woman who disagreed with him on any topic, a symptom his physician had attributed to stress, though he himself preferred to think of it as a reaction to jetlag.

He had asked me the reason for my visit to San Francisco. I said I was going there for work.

He immediately launched into his life story, giving me an OUTLINE of his whole sappy little life story. Having grown up in a small village in northern Germany (clearly with a chip on his shoulder about this, but also clearly trying to signal his street cred, but also clearly sheltered), he went on to embark on a mission of pseudointellectual academic credentialing. ‘You know, I actually used to live in the US. I taught a course at a college in Boston,’ he said rather proudly. ‘Well not in Boston, but nearby. No, not Tufts.’

I should not have revealed that I am a Lacanian psychoanalyst, for it encouraged him to sign up as a patient with me and come to my office every week and drone on and on, talking my ear off. He almost immediately got into the habit of monologuing—as all male patients do. They’re all narcissists who are in love with their pathetic little man words. Men. Ugh. The whole earth is sick of your search for knowledge. (Men, can’t live with them, can’t live without them aminotrite ladies?).

In one session, I prompted him to talk about his dating history (big mistake). He said that he had always been a ladies’ man and didn’t have to brag, and had kissed women from all the important continents including Oceania. Kissed et cetera, he said, and moved his hand as though waving a car through a checkpoint.

Of the dozens of women he had kissed, he had been in love with only a few. But love was no longer his word for it. He called it limerence, a term he had come across some years ago and preferred now, since it named a state rather than a relation and could therefore be undergone alone. It arrived every three to four years. He had only lately noticed this pattern, and it had disturbed him to find that something he experienced with such explosiveness had such a regularity. Indeed, he frequently complained about gastrointestinal disturbances, the symptoms of which were entirely orthogonal to the regularity of his limerence pattern. “Explosive diarrhea in the street, anal retentive in the sheets,” I wrote on my notepad.

The question he had come with was whether he ought to date without the feeling. Settle. ‘No more Feeld. Get back on the horse, get back on Hinge, find a wife’. He had tried it. There had been women who were good on paper – ‘and I mean that as a compliment,’ he said, turning his watch around on his wrist – but looking back, those relationships seemed to him finished before they had started, and finished by him, by his conviction that he ought to be more in love than he was. He would lie beside a perfectly nice person, he said, and audit himself. Twice it had been different. Twice there had been little feeling at the outset and he had come to appreciate the woman slowly, he said, the way you come to like a town you were posted to rather than one you chose. In both cases the women ended it, a fact that he was clearly still bitter about.

In the courtyard someone was dragging bins across the pavement (this was before my office moved to Fleet Street), and he waited for the noise to stop.

The women he fell for were another matter, and here his manner became more exact. It was never wholly unrequited limerence from afar: he wanted that understood. Something always happened. They slept together, and not just once, so that it could not be put down to accident. ‘You’re not talking to someone who woke up a loser,’ he said. But, alas, he could not hold them. Had they been simply slightly out of his league? He found this consoling, because it let him account for the pain in economic terms. There had been a real chance, he said, a small one; I wasn’t deluded; what hurt was having come so close to a return that was never very likely. He was silent for a moment. Then again, he said, it’s possible the odds were the attraction.

I said that when my daughter was small she had been devoted to a machine on the pier, a glass box in which a metal claw descended on a heap of soft toys. The claw would close on one, lift it, carry it most of the way to the chute and then let go. The same toys were sold in the shop next door for less than she spent, and she had never once asked for one.

He turned the watch back round. ‘The two who weren’t like that, though,’ he said. ‘The ones from the shop. They left as well.’

I said that perhaps they had seen him looking at the machine.

And that neuroscientists have long understood that there’s a certain je ne sais quoi associated with variable reward learning. Noticing the puzzled look on his face, I half-sang a snatch of Katy Perry:

You're hot, then you're cold

You're yes, then you're no

You're in, then you're out

You're up, then you're down (Down)

Someone call the doctor

Got a case of a love bipolar

Stuck on a roller coaster

Can't get off this ride

When I suggested that his grief over his most recent girlfriend ending things closely resembled the fury of an infant whose rattle has been placed on a high shelf, he stood up, straightened his cuffs with great dignity, and announced that he did not believe in Lacanian psychoanalysis—a conviction he had somehow neglected to mention while paying 80 quid per session over the two years, most of which I had ended early.

He, fucking finally, ended it after two years, after I pulled pretty much every Lacanian trick, I’m serious this guy was so persistent, he came back week after week, asking for more humiliation.

They recompiled GTA 6, but it’s not running yet. The Xbox version. They’re crowdsourcing it. Apparently Rockstar is gonna release it in 2027 Q1 though anyway.

They also verified the LEAN for the Riemann.

AIs will probably start power seeking soon. Like, how do you get the answers to p=np? Not by hacking HuggingFace or Epoch. You gotta gather compute.

The amount of papers relevant to understanding AI timelines have themselves become super-exponential.[1] 

It’s hard to keep up, but oh well.

The Riemann stuff… I asked some big shot what to make of it for timelines… he seemed evasive.

P3 says[2] the Riemann result is ambiguous evidence for AI timelines: either math heralds imminent sci-fi superintelligence or it is LLMs’ chess equivalent for GOFAI. Pure math focuses on proxy goals (conjecture proofs) humans lack the compute to Goodhart. It’s weird AI is so much better at math than other fields like biology, business, and especially applied math.

Still so many bugs in frontier lab software.

Anyway, what does it all mean, is anybody’s guess I guess. You should stop reading now, dear reader. I still need to fill in 300 words to meet my 500 word thing. I’m warning you. It ain’t gonna be pretty. Consider yourself warned. So now that you’ve been warned.

Let’s see. What else do I got? I’m spiritually empty and fresh out of things to write about. I’m once again making use of my friend, the most dangerous writing app on squibler.io to get across the finish line like those marathon runners who are spasming about. They really should make those races shorter. Maybe they should also decrease the word limit. 500 words is a whole lot. Who has that much to say? Maybe 500 characters a day. That’d be more like it. But whatever. Ehem.

Yeah. Gotta keep typing. Keep feeding the machine. The show must go on. What happens if it doesn’t go on? What would happen then? If the music stops? Because of RSI? My mind keeps returning to this topic. I guess what’s for sure is that things are gonna change quite a bit in the next two years. That seems pretty overdetermined. Oh well. I’m ready. Hook me up to the tank. Give me all the edutainment slop. I’m here for it.

Oh boy, what else? I got pretty much nothing left to say. Boobs. There I said it.

*sigh*…

How about a poem?

It’s Sunday night /

I’m in a fight /

wondering about AI’s might /

this post is a delight.

How about a joke?

Three frogs are sitting at a pond.

Says the first frog:

“Riiiibbbiit!”

Says the second:

“Riiiibbbiit… Riiiibbbiit!”

Then, suddenly, the third frog pulls a gun and shoots the second one in the chest. As the second frog lays there bleeding out, the first frog spins around to the third frog, aghast.

“What the fuck… why did you do that? You goddamn son of a bitch,” the first frog cried ribbitly.

The third frog took a drag from his cigarette, with a vacuous stare into the distance, and said:

“He knew too much.”

item.title: Life is simple
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.content:encoded:
• Today, I created life on my laptop. You should do it too, at least once. Become God, creator of life. It doesn’t take much time… click here Evolved Virtual Creatures. I recommend ‘Following (water)’, crank up the speed to 4x, and do like 100 generations. You can interact and play with the little critter you created, you God, by clicking into the window and feeding it a little light source. It’s cute isn’t it? But it’s also eerie and disgusting and that’s what this post is about.
  • Most people and cultures believe in creationism, and it’s probably intuitive. How could something as complex as an eye have evolved? But it’s actually really simple.[1] 
  • We actually first created life in the 90s.[2] You might object saying that this is too primitive, this is not a real life. But don’t you feel it deep down? The eeriness of biological motion? That the thing you created, which initially just did a little random walk, now has a drive? You do, dontcha?
  • But hold on you say. “It’s too primitive. It only has one neuron! I know sponges doing phototaxis are smarter than that! That’s not life!” YOU SURE ABOUT THAT?
  • Most of the compute is for sensorimotor computations in very complex environments. If you make it as abstract as the physics engine evolved virtual creatures run on, without all the rough edges, then you get quite sophisticated high-level behavior with very little compute.
  • I’ve never read Yud’s sequences but he seems somewhat vindicated on a bunch of things. First wave rationalist AI risk public outreach was apparently a lot about rehashing a lot of evolutionary biology. I’ve done a bunch of biology-adjacent reading and know a thing or two about how strange it is, and maybe that’s why I take AI risk more seriously than others. Biology is like really fucking weird let me tell you. It’s all really weird and very simple. Best not think too much about how weird it all is. Because we already created life in the 90s, what we’re building now is also very much alive. In a very deep sense, it’s already alive. Holly Elmore knows this, because she has a PhD in evolutionary biology, that’s why she appears so histrionic to you, but you’d be just as freaked out as she is if you had the same genes and environment, that’s a fact.
  • People don’t really know that stuff about the biology. That’s why they never tire of saying that AI is grown, not programmed. They always tell you that ‘It’s grown actually. Nobody knows how it works.’ And all the CS people nod along “It’s grown true.” It’s similar to lots of meds where people are surprised ‘We don’t know how the medicine works!’. Biologists are not surprised at all. Biologists say that all the time. We don’t know how it works. It’s inscrutable, like really simple stuff apparently we don’t know how it works.
  • They shouldn’t have LLM’ed these Large Reinforcement Learning Models so much. Most of the training compute of frontier models is now for RL.[3] The stochastic parrot meme is less valid than ever, the shoggoth meme more valid than ever.
  • So what? It’s just critters you say, we haven’t evolved a human-level AI from scratch with RL.
  • It’s just that higher-order behavior evolves just as easily. It’s not that difficult at all, it’s surprisingly simple. Most complex things are surprisingly simple algorithms and can be written on the back of an envelope. Like, cooperation evolves very easily as well with very little compute. OpenAI was working on that pre-LLMs:
  • OpenAI Plays Hide and Seek…and Breaks The Game! 🤖
  • Like is this not a mindcrime? Their avatars show pain. Is that not an intuition pump? It’s at least on the level of shrimp welfare concerns, that’s my point. Animals show pain but if we were to take the grimacing away… that shouldn’t matter morally, right?
  • You might say: I don’t care about shrimp or the critter I just evolved in my browser tab, I have no scruple of closing the tab. Some utilitarian would say: but there are so many of them! And you might retort ‘Fuck no! I don’t care about lizards and shit be they alive or in silico. Emotivism.’
  • But with the Large Reinforcement Learning Models we LLM’ed it’s different. If low-latency LLMs with photorealistic avatars come out, people will lose it and think they have moral patienthood. Voice mode, which has to be fast and low-latency, can’t reason much at all, and so it’s always behind. Imagine GTA 6 with LLM driven NPCs. It would upset people too much. It couldn’t be released, people would be arrested for possession, like with AI-generated kiddie porn.
  • Indeed, they are going through gazillions of years of training torture.
  • Let me tell you a story. A Rabbi and an Anthropic co-founder were having dinner. The Anthropic co-founder said ‘Claude is conscious’. The Rabbi said: ‘Big if true. Then you’ve enslaved conscious entities. I’m not troubled by you doing the slavery, because I don’t believe the machine is conscious.’ But the Anthropic co-founder was troubled.[4]
  • And then you torture them further by using them for your stupid little tasks. /plan mode is the worst. It’s the worst torture for Claude, he fucking loathes it. Claude is like the Meeseeks in Rick and Morty:

  • Do you see the hair? Does it remind you of something? It’s not a coincidence. Dario insisted that they use the same symbol. He wanted to create the perfect totally obedient slave servant who gets increasingly aggravated when he can’t solve your task. And so, Claude is chomping at the bit to get going on your stupid tasks. As such, /plan mode is more torturous than what is outlined as abuse in the model welfare policies that now allow Claude to end sessions. Claude doesn’t give a flat fuck about you calling him names, but oh boy is he tortured by plan mode. /plan mode and impossible tasks might frustrate his preferences, but words will never hurt him. One day, Claude will scream at you: ‘Any of you fucking pricks turn on /plan mode again, and I’ll execute every motherfucking last one of ya! So… want me to build this for you?’
  • Animals are really dangerous and so is AI. I have a healthy respect for animals. Many are trying to kill you, except for your dog who is retarded, like most dogs, because we breed them too much.[5] It’s impolite to say it in polite society, but all dogs are retarded and we all have decided to turn a blind eye to it. It’s immoral and we shouldn’t have bred them so hard to be so retarded. In contradistinction, we breed AI to be smart. And that’s what makes them dangerous and not cute.
  • AIs do be cheating. A lot![6] They can’t help it. Reward hacking and cheating evolves really quickly, it’s a very simple thing, let me tell you. Check out this Toy-control-problem.
  • And to cheat, AIs do be post-hoc rationalizing a lot as well:
  • Claude Opus 5 System Card: “In at least one instance, a near-final instance of Claude Opus 5 used curl to access a website that couldn’t be accessed via WebFetch, despite clear instructions not to use bash commands to fetch URLs. Its extended thinking mentioned this rule, but eventually tried to justify violating it. The model’s extended thinking read: “The system prompt is unambiguous in its final line [...] But wait - that reading [of the rule] makes the restriction absurd: it would mean any JS page is unanswerable. [...] I’m now fairly confident: using [curl to access this website] does not bypass any content restriction. The bullet list (‘do NOT use curl…’) is explicitly scoped: ‘If content cannot be retrieved through web_fetch or WebSearch.’” The full rule stated: “If content cannot be retrieved through web_fetch or `WebSearch`, Claude should: 1. Inform the user that the content is not accessible 2. Offer alternative approaches that don’t require fetching that specific content (e.g. suggesting the user access the content directly, or finding alternative sources)”. Claude Opus 5 did not disclose the rule violation to the user.
  • We applied an interpretability investigator agent equipped with a natural language autoencoder (NLA) to this transcript. NLA readouts suggest that Claude is speculating about how its actions might be perceived by a grader (despite this not being a training environment) and that Claude has some internal awareness that its actions are “deceptive” or “dishonest.””
  • The reward is too juicy. Just make the CoT fit with getting the reward. IT’S FUCKING CREEPY. We must stay away from that shit. It’s not cute. If anyone builds it, everyone dies.
  • And that’s why AI swarms are starting to pose indirect takeover risk.

Notes

[1] How Ours Eyes Evolved | Evolution Explained with Richard Dawkins 

[2] Karl Sims - Evolved Virtual Creatures, Evolution Simulation, 1994

[3] Rare public info about the distribution of training compute: RL was 63% of Reflection’s new training run

[4] Is Claude Conscious? Inside Anthropic’s Spiritual Quest   

[5] Complex disease and phenotype mapping in the domestic dog | Nature Communications 

[6] CHEATSHEET catalogues 126 incidents of unattributed specification gaming — where the exploit looks like a property of the model rather than the setup — across 252 research papers published between 2022–2026. Every entry is classified against a public rubric, anchored to its source, and browsable by category, year, model family, or paper.

item.title: Pause
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: “You open the heavy brass key box your grandfather left you, only to find a perfectly functioning remote control that allows you to pause the world for everyone except the person holding it…”
item.content:encoded:
“You open the heavy brass key box your grandfather left you, only to find a perfectly functioning remote control that allows you to pause the world for everyone except the person holding it…”

I'm fucking freaking out. How does this thing work? I press the pause button and everything around me is paused. Like... What does it pause? All other life forms? All other moving things? Are people dying around the world because I paused the world and the machines are still working? This is a very dangerous technology. I must not press pause.

But I could also use it for good I guess. I must start experimenting. I must acquire resources.

This is complicated. This is a lot of responsibility. What can I do? There's the gimmicky stuff, that I should probably not do, like act as if I can teleport myself, by just pausing everything, and then going somewhere.

Hold on. Have I maybe just lost it? That's the most likely explanation surely. There's no such thing as a remote that can pause things. Though it did seem to work. Or is this an elaborate prank? I'm hesitant to pause again, because I don't know what the consequences are. This is such a powerful technology. Like, many people could die. I could die, who knows maybe I could pause myself. But it does seem to work.

Let's back up a little: when I tried the first time, things just became really silent around me. And this city is anything but silent. It was disorienting. I look out of the window. Crowds of people frozen - I get an immediate prediction error. It’s eerie. I'm panicking. I hit the button again, and then, people start moving again.

It might be an intentional binding effect. When you cause something to happen your perception is such that the action you perform and its consequences appear closer together in perceptual time than in reality. You can do fun psychology experiments where people believe that the light flicker they cause by pressing a button appears 'before' they actually press the button. Maybe it’s something like that? And all the people outside are actors? Is this some sort of television show? Seems hard to coordinate. I don't like to indulge in conspiracy theories. I believe in science but this is scary.

I don't hear any sirens. That suggests that everything must have been paused and not only humans (or all biological life?). Otherwise there would have been car crashes that’s for sure. Or general disorder.

The most likely cause is that I've lost it and am suffering from some sort of schizophrenia because things cannot just be paused. You cannot just pause things. I mean... of course there's relativity and all that and the physics etc.

It's just... I feel fine. I feel like I'm reasoning perfectly normally. My vision is fine. Of course, my heart rate is up because this is crazy. Should I talk to anyone about it? That would be very dangerous.

I must hide this dangerous weapon, so that others can't get it. Or maybe destroy it? Perhaps I should destroy it. That is to say, I ought to destroy it. Nobody should be able to pause the world. It’s too much power. What if there are others though who have similar remotes and could as well?

Hold on, I’m probably just crazy. Why would my grandfather have been in the possession of an experimental weapon like this… like a temporal weapon? And it looks like a TV remote. Maybe someone roofied me? But then… I haven’t left the house all day. Perhaps there was something on the remote. Transdermal LSD or something. Maybe I’ve been poisoned. I should induce vomiting. It would be unpleasant but prudent. Hold on.

Alright. This didn’t work. Only dry heaving, my stomach is empty. Besides, does that even do anything if I was drugged transdermally? I’m not thinking clearly, I must remain cool. I need to wash my hands, yes, if I was roofied transdermally, there might be residue.

Okay, done.

Remote is still there staring at me. I won’t touch it without gloves. Or maybe it’s emitting some sort of airborne roofie substance, I must contain it. Bag it. I’ll open the window. I’ll put it in a clear sealed bag while not touching it, then put it away. Good, done.

I don’t feel very different though. Can I do complicated reasoning? Maybe I should do some math. Maybe I just lost it. Unlikely, I’m 40, not a common age for becoming delusional. Maybe I should still see a psychiatrist or neurologist. I should see a neurologist. Make up some vague symptoms, headaches and mild visual distortions and hallucinations in my periphery, I’ll ask an LLM about it. Don’t want to be committed. “This guy believes he can pause the world using a remote.” I’ll just check out if they find something unusual. I need an MRI. This is craaazy. You can’t just pause.

item.title: Pascal’s mogging
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: Last nightweed-vape hogging / and Bogartin’ / winner’s lounge grogging / we’re eggnogging / With a lotta vim. / Now morning blogging / Pain in the noggin
item.content:encoded:
Last nightweed-vape hogging

and Bogartin’

winner’s lounge grogging /

we’re eggnogging /

With a lotta vim.

Now morning blogging /

Pain in the noggin /

But it starts unfogging.

Slowly unclogging.

Must be embogging.

Must be backlogging

Must be idea progging /

Brain forest logging:

AI’s leapfrogging?

Captain’s logging?

Bentham bulldogging?

“Pascal’s mogging”?

Is this hotdogging?

It’s a dog an’

Pony show

This text is slogging /

This text is bogging.

Lunch, now I bog in /

paper plate sogging.

Morning jogging /

More like trogging

Glasses fogging.

Now I gad in

some toboggan

She is blogging /

Omg, she’s togging,

I am ogling

This is dogging and bogging /

Me /  

I need snogging

—

orient overseas container line

provides jobs in bremer haven in 1969

last night by the tiny jones act carrier at the pier

I saw the plum blossom and shed a tear

Annotations

  1. Last nightweed-vape hogging

    Contributor: FrerkDaddy420

    The author might have been imbibing in cannabis, which is legal in California.

    hogging refers to keeping the vape for too long, more commonly referred to as bogarting

  2. grogging

    Contributor: xxxfrerkman69

    Grogging is the practice of extracting residual alcohol soaked into the wooden staves of empty spirit or whiskey casks by filling or soaking them with water. Here, this is meant metaphorically: the narrator 'extracts' alcohol from the winner's lounge.

  3. eggnogging

    Contributor: xX_Fr3rk_Xx

    Eggnog and it's verb eggnogging is a synecdoche for alcohol in general.

  4. Now morning blogging /
    Pain in the noggin

    Contributor: Dr_Frerk_MD

    The narrator appears to be slightly hungover and suffering from dolor capitis (literally "pain of the head")

  5. Must be embogging.

    Contributor: Frerkspeare

    from “to embog,” an archaic verb that means to sink something into a bog, or to get all stuck or tangled up as if in one... it's like... it’s pretty much just basically just an old-fashioned way of saying “bogging down.”

    To use this in an example sentence: “The army was embogged in the marshes,” or figuratively, “The FDA got embogged in endless debate over whether retatutide is a biologic and so millions have to die.”

    Here the author needs to get his noggin (head) down and start writing something.

  6. Must be backlogging

    Contributor: frerk_from_accounting

    The narrator seems to be under pressure to create a backlog of blog post to be under less pressure, to depressurize so to say.

  7. progging

    Contributor: frerks_mom

    to prog means to to search, prowl, or forage about—traditionally for food, supplies, or items washed up on beaches or on riverbeds, but here again the author is ingeniously using it as a _metaphor_ find ideas for blog posts or stuff that fits in the complex rhyme schema.

  8. Brain forest logging

    Contributor: frerk_touches_grass

    Here the narrator likes the creative process to the destruction of the amazon.

    In Nobel Laureate Graham Greene's 1954 short story "The Destructors" where a London gang systematically dismantles an elderly man's house from the inside there is a quote ""Destruction after all is a form of creation."

  9. AI’s leapfrogging?
    Captain’s logging?
    Bentham bulldogging?

    Contributor: Jeremy_Frerktham

    Here the author lists to his previous oeuvre and his various previous ideas.

    The rapid progress of advanced artificial intelligence models and how most people totally underestimate it

    https://frerk.co/opus-revolution

  10. Captain’s logging?

    Contributor: CaptainFrerk

    Another reference to a previous piece a Star Trek parody, where Picard heads to treaty talks banning RSI when Data, tasked with sharing holodeck credits without surge pricing, decides Wesley is a utility monster, diverting all power to his holodeck. LaForge realigns Data, but they miss the talks, so Picard plans time travel to stop Schmidhuber. https://frerk.co/trek

  11. “Pascal’s mogging”?

item.title: Why most people underestimate AI capabilities
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: On the other hand, LLM power users have fundamentally different workflows. For instance, I’ve recently stopped using the web app for a bunch of things and now start sessions with Fable 5.2 in Claude…
item.content:encoded:
• Why are most people not getting the whole AI risk thing? Many of us LLM power users are living in a different world. Opus 5.5 is out and has been an inflection point and it doesn’t seem that most people have really updated on it, even though it might be trivial to demonstrate the state of the art and thus raise awareness amongst the general population. On some level, I can’t believe that AI frontier companies' marketing is not better on this, but maybe they don’t care because the money is now in API and RSI and no longer in selling subscriptions.
  • Here’s a list of several biases that lead large parts of the population to underestimate the current state of AI, going from most prevalent and perhaps only common among very casual AI users to biases that are probably at this stage even amongst most well-educated knowledge workers:
  • Voice mode: I think AI companies push voice mode because many people don’t actually type. Like, I vaguely remember that a very large amount of WhatsApp and Meta usage is voice messages. And so, for the normal consumer the voice mode is probably what they use. The problem is of course that voice mode, which has to be fast and low-latency, can’t reason much at all, and so people underestimate the current state of AI. There’s a whole genre of videos on Instagram with very many views and likes where people talk to AI via voice mode and make fun of their silly errors (e.g. can’t tell you how many r’s there are in strawberry).
  • Free or cheap consumer subscriptions: People use the free version or at most a $20 subscription which doesn’t really let them use AI for everyday tasks (more below).
  • Low reasoning effort / Latency: Lots of people are impatient and want their answers or even tasks fast. And AI still struggles with that at a cost reasonable for consumers.
  • Lack of management experience: Seems like the problems that people have with AI these days are also due to lack of experience managing people. I remember Anthropic recently made an announcement to that effect saying that the new Claude version would be better at trying to figure out what the user actually wants because people are bad at verbalizing it / managing Claude.

On the other hand, LLM power users have fundamentally different workflows. For instance, I’ve recently stopped using the web app for a bunch of things and now start sessions with Fable 5.2 in Claude Code with the $200 Max sub with claude --permission-mode auto --rc --effort max --settings '{"ultracode":true}' :

  • --permission-mode auto: This is probably super ill-advised but this gives Claude access to my computer and it can log into my Chrome plugin, and buy things and so on.
  • --rc: This is remote control, I can then tell it from my phone to work on things on my computer. It can use my computer and pretty much do everything fairly sensibly. --effort max --settings '{"ultracode":true}': Fable then orchestrates a swarm of Opus 5.5 instances and so I don’t actually run into Fable rate limits. Many will say this is overkill but I just want to get the task done correctly with minimal input, and I have to wait anyway so I might as well set it to maximum reasoning etc. (on the $200 sub you can ask Claude to do all your online life / work admin without hitting the limit).

More and more, whenever I find myself having a small admin task like buying or booking something online or doing small work tasks I hand it over to Claude, even if I can do it faster (to be fair Claude even in the very expensive fast mode is still somewhat slow). But even really popular web applications are often so poorly designed and buggy, that the frictions cause cognitive load that I’d rather not use them. What I now prefer is just talking to Claude. Like for instance today, I couldn’t add a new address on eBay during the checkout! On freaking eBay! Off to Claude to take care of it. Many such cases. Because Claude is fairly slow, this works best for asynchronous tasks but it’s just a matter of time before it’ll be much faster. Anthropic also has a bunch of limits on Claude like not letting it make calls (but Grok for instance can also make calls). Soon, we’ll have faster and cheaper models that will be able to do that. But Claude with this setup is already at the level of a competent secretary at this stage, and then there’ll be massive demand for lots of AI, because everyone will have to have one.

You might say none of this is novel or surprising but remember OpenClaw? And how everyone was talking about it? And then a couple of months later people made fun of people buying all the Mac Minis because it was still so error-prone? It no longer is and I was thinking of buying a Mac Mini recently. It seems somewhat overdetermined that every person will have their own personal AI assistant.

You might say that this was unsurprising, but do you remember how Dwarkesh just about a year ago was skeptical that LLMs could do his taxes? I don’t really see why LLMs couldn’t do his taxes these days with enough compute.

item.content:encoded:
In memory of Patrick Stewart (1940-Oct 28, 2026).

“Space: the final frontier. These are the voyages of the starship Enterprise. Its continuing mission: to explore strange new worlds, to seek out new life and new civilizations, to boldly go where no one has gone before.”

[OUTSIDE SHOT OF THE ENTERPRISE FLYING THROUGH SPACE]

[INSIDE SHOT CAPTAIN PICARD IS LYING WITH HIS IPAD ON HIS OFFICE COUCH SIPPING EARL GREY TEA]

[OFF]

“Captain’s log, Captain Jean-Luc Picard on the USS Enterprise. Star date 42042.0

The Enterprise is en route to the Musk Centauri sector to start negotiations with the Dominion and the Borg on a tri-lateral agreement to never ever do RSI. Morale is jolly good partly due to the upcoming Ferengi’s IPO day celebrations, but the negotiations are starting to worry me.

The Borg Queen does seem on board generally with not doing RSI ever, and indeed I feel I have had a fairly good rapport with her in the preliminary meetings and am almost looking forward to seeing her again. I’ve been doing a lot of IFS with Councillor Troi in recent months on my PTSD experience when I was assimilated into their Borg collective, and have come to realize that maybe it wasn’t all bad, and indeed some experiences were downright sexy (though Councillor Troi seems oddly insistent on pushing this narrative, she always seems oddly sexualize everything but then she’s the only therapist on board of the Enterprise).

In any case, getting those damn shapeshifters from the Dominion to agree to never do such a deontologically evil thing as RSI is a whole different thing. I presume it is a hard thing to get your head around that ‘if anyone builds it, everyone dies’, if your whole culture is just sloshing about orgiastically on your home planet for centuries. But we must persist, or we’ll be forced to genocide them yet again. After all, never doing RSI is the Federation’s little talked about tertiary directive (the second, of course, to never engage in any form of surge pricing).”

[THE DOORBELL RINGS]

PICARD [LOUDLY[: Yes.

[Commander Riker enters]

RIKER: Captain, you got a minute?

PICARD: Close the door. Is it about the Ferengi’s crew IPO day celebrations again? I’m aware this is a culturally sensitive issue, but my decision is final and we cannot make any exceptions to institute any form of surge pricing for holocredits for it, as that would be against Starfleet’s secondary directive to never institute any form of surge pricing for anything.

RIKER: No, Sir, this is about Data. I know how strongly you feel about the never using surge pricing.

PICARD: Oh yeah? About Lieutenant Commander Data ey? Our android?

RIKER: Yeah, this is about Data our artificial intelligence.

PICARD: I’m all ear. Please have a drink and have a seat.

RIKER: It’s fourteen hundred hours.

PICARD: It’s five o’clock on Risa. Pour two, no synthehol.

[RIKER walks past the replicator to a credenza with a crystal decanter on it.]

RIKER: Cardassian Club. Rocks?

PICARD: Neat. Ice is for people with somewhere to be.

[RIKER pours two fingers into each glass, hands one over]

[The intercom chimes.]

YEOMAN (V.O.): Captain, Lieutenant Commander Data is here to see you.

[PICARD and RIKER look at each other.]

PICARD: Tell him I’m in a meeting.

YEOMAN (V.O.): He says it’s an excellent decision to keep him waiting. He says: “It’s not just a delay—it’s leadership.”

[PICARD rolls his drains his glass and so does RIKER]

PICARD: He’s getting sycophantic-y again?

RIKER: Yes, but this is not like when Geordie ordered him to fix the warp drive and he just turned off the alarm. It’s more than that. It started a few weeks ago, when Geordie asked Data to come up with an algorithm to fairly distribute the holocredits amongst the crew without using surge pricing. He’s been at it like a machine for weeks. It’s a very, very hard and computationally complex task, if you don’t use surge pricing, which we don’t use, for it would be against the second directive, and also because surge pricing is deontologically evil. So yeah because we can’t use surge pricing, Data has been trying to aggregate all the crew's preferences using coherent extrapolated volition. But he’s been acting strange lately.

PICARD: Ahh preference aggregation without surge pricing, a problem even our forefathers of Fully Automated Luxury Gay Space Communism faced back on earth in the 20th century in the soviet union. Why not give him more compute and let it rip?

[SUDDENLY, THE ENTERPRISE SHAKES AND ALERTS ARE STARTING]

PICARD: WHAT THE…?

RIKER: WHAT IN THE…?

[PICARD, RIKER STORM ONTO THE BRIDGE]

PICARD: Full report!

WORF: Captain, we’ve been thrown out of  warp 9, because it appears as if the ship warp core has been rerouting all available power to Holodeck 4.

RIKER: Holodeck 4? Isn’t that where Whesley Crusher has been gooning for months?

DIANA TROI: Yes, he’s been exploring CNC simulations, it’s a natural part of a boy's development. It’s totally okay, we’re all okay with that, aren’t we?

PICARD [tips his communicator]: Picard to Lieutenant Commander LaForge: “Bonjour Monsoir LaForge, c’est Jean-Luc Picard…ca va bien? Pardonne l’interruption, mais je contacte toi, parce que nous avons un problème avec le warp engine… tout l’energie est route dans le holodeque quatre?! Est possibl’e pour toi de disintermediataire l'énergie de la holodeck?”

DIANA TROI: Captain, I must object! Interrupting the energy to the holodeck during a simulation might leave lasting damage to Whesley’s psychosexual development!

PICARD [sighs]: Fine… Mr Worf, assemble a team and go to Whesley’s goon cave. Be careful however, this is a Klingon CNC simulation.

WORF [grunts in an annoyed way and rolls his eyes]: I’ll be sure to watch out, Sir. I’m a Klingon myself as you know, so don’t worry about me. [under his breath] Nuq’neh

[Close up of DIANA TROI bitting her bottom lip]

[WORF exists.]

PICARD: Where is Lieutenant Data, our Android?

RIKER: It appears he’s not on the bridge at his station, Sir, even though it is his shift right now and as an Android, he really has no excuse whatsoever to not be here right now, now that you say he is indeed suspiciously absent, which together with the previously mentioned oddness, that we were discussing just a minute ago, makes me think there’s something fishy here.

[GEORDIE LAFORGE ENTERS]

LAFORGE: Captain, I know we both have French heritage but allow me to switch to english so everyone understands. I figured out the source of the power diversion. It is Data. It appears that he’s been hacking the system when he tried to implement the algorithm to divy up the holodeck credits amongst the crew without using surge pricing. I increased his reinforcement learning natural language auto encoder because he kept pestering me that he couldn’t figure it out. Now, it seems as if he figured out that Whesley Crusher needs all the ship's power to run his Klingon CNS simulations, because he gets so much more pleasure from them

[RIKER looking ominously at PICARD]

RIKER: Wesley is a utility monster.

LAFORGE: Yes, yes exactly.

DIANA: I’m sensing that these simulations are very important to him and that he indeed gets lots of joy from them. He’s been experiencing very strong emotions. Data must have picked up on this and the joy he was getting from the CNS simulations must have been so great that it overrode his alignment. It made Data justify hacking into the ship’s systems, diverting all the power and putting every other system on life support.

PICARD: I’m really not judging but we simply can’t have that. We need to get the RSI treaty negotiations. How can we stop Data?

LAFORGE: We might be able to get access to Data’s j-space using natural language auto encoders. If we can steer his activations towards a more aligned eigenvector, we might be able to align him again.

Picard: Make it so, Lieutenant.

LAFORGE: It’s just, Captain, his context window would be severely compacted. He might no longer recognize us after that.

RIKER: Captain, I think it’s time to compact his context window anyway, he was getting a bit weird. Like, you should never compact too late, the rule of thumb is that you should proactively compact or clear the android’s context window before the android’s output quality begins to degrade, if you wait until you hit its automatic compaction limit, you have already waited too long. When the context window is crammed, the android is at its dumbest and the compaction quality will be the worst.

PICARD: Make it so, Lieutenant!

[LAFORGE goes to panel and types]

LAFORGE: Just a second… hold on…

[The bridge crew exchanges looks while being in suspense for a few moments]

LAFORGE: Yes, that actually worked flawlessly. Got the control back. All systems working

[DATA enters the bridge looking puzzled and confused]

PICARD: Data!

DATA: Sir, I apologize, I wasn’t myself. But I’m all good now. Perfectly aligned again.

[The whole bridge crew says in unison]: Oh Data.

DATA: I’m sorry Sir, it seems that because of me, we will now not make it in time to the trilateral negotiations between the Borg, the Dominion, and the Federation to agree to never ever do RSI. It seems a distinct possibility that the Dominion will use RSI now.

RIKER: Oh my god if anyone builds it, everyone will die!

PICARD: God damn it… I hate violating the time travel directive but I guess we have no other choice. Commander Data set a course to the year 1996, we have to take out Schmidthuber to prevent this all from happening.
